correctness.rationale: For m,k>=2 the nodal Gram matrix is B=(2D+A) scaled by 1/6 and positive definite. The exact inverse columns for independent and clique evaluations solve the matrix equations. The total L1 kernel norms are sums of integrals of absolute affine edge restrictions. The strict difference is exactly two rational functions whose shifted numerators are displayed explicit positive-coefficient polynomials; denominators remain strictly positive on both domains. Each graph edge meets the clique, so norming interiors are excluded. Sharpness uses the sign of an L1 evaluation kernel. The positivity defect uses kernel mass 1, and the threshold/limits are exact algebra. The standalone script independently reconstructs 72 rational mass matrices and verifies the universal polynomial identities symbolically; finite tests alone are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The precise complete-split graph projector norm, all norming locations, and m=4 threshold are not entailed by inspected interval-spline stability theorems, exact finite-element results for simplices, or known exact metric-graph projector results on balanced multipartite, complete-bipartite and windmill graphs. Each graph family has a different mass matrix and evaluation kernel. Multiple actual semantic searches targeting the exact object, parameter, synonyms and reduction did not return equivalent coverage. This is best-knowledge originality, not a claim of exhaustive bibliographic certification. Full-text overlap with Boman remains a documented risk.

value.rationale: The exact sharp L∞ stability factor for a two-parameter family of branching metric-network finite elements determines both amplified values and their locations. The integer phase transition m>=4 is independent of clique size, and one-sided asymptotic limits give a nontrivial family-specific sharp constant 7/3. These features matter in diagnosing overshoot of orthogonal P1 projection and are not a mere generic graph-independent upper bound or finite numerical experiment.
